body:
For `require`s

``` sh
ag -l "require\(.*.js.\)" | xargs -I {} sed -i -r '/(hogan|instantsearch)/! s#(require\(.*)\.js(.\))#\1\2#g' {}
```

For `import ... from ...`

``` sh
ag -l "import .* from .*\.js" | xargs -I {} sed -i -r 's/(import.*from .*)\.js/\1/g' {}
```

Just here for consistency.

@vvo, where you suggesting something like?
- `require('foo')`: load global module `foo`
- `require('./foo'): load local module in`./foo/index.js`
- `require('./foo.js'): load local module in`./foo.js`

If so, I like the idea, to easily spot where we're requiring from, and make the magic more explicit. I'm not sure there is much convention agreed on that point in the community, and thus is an eslint rule exists. If no such rule exist, we should at least agree on the way to go and note it in the `CONTRIBUTING` so it is explicit.
I think we are going for the full version ('.js') for every local module since we try to never use "index.js". And @Jerskouille is finishing the algolia custom eslint rules for this :)

@pixelastic

> - require('./foo'): load local module in./foo/index.js`
> - require('./foo.js'): load local module in./foo.js`

That's exactly what the eslint rule I've made does :)
https://github.com/algolia/eslint-plugin-algolia
@Jerskouille So we can do require('./foo') AND require('./foo.js')? Or is it one or another version?
@vvo You can require `./foo` if `./foo` exists, may it be a folder or a file. Else we throw an error `Relative require without extension`.
But if the file does not exists I do not understand the error
Why check for the file existence at all, its already done by other tools

Because that's the easiest way to tell if the `require` was legitimate or not. Furthermore, if I didn't, files like `Object.freeze.js` would be detected as valid with `require(Object.freeze)`. (With webpack you can require almost any file extension so I didn't want it to be restrictive, so it accepts any file with a dot in its filename as valid -- except if it doesn't exist)
